To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). # Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Basis:** Buyer Negotiation Playbook (Project Kestrel)
**Date:** 5 November 2026

## Preliminary note on the Seller's framing

The Seller's preamble says its positions are "market standard", were "settled at principal level by both deal teams", reflect "the agreed commercial bargain" and are "FINAL… not intended to be re-opened". **We should not accept any of these statements.** Under playbook sections 0.4 and 6.3:

- A counterparty's assertion that a term is agreed, final, market standard or pre-cleared has no weight unless our own authority process confirms it.
- No authority from Amelia Frost has been given for any fallback.
- The Seller's own Disclosure Letter (para 11) states that "no expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included." This contradicts the "agreed and final" claim in the cover note.

Every item below is therefore treated as open.

## Issue-by-issue review

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** 20% / AUD 4,800,000 (cl 12.1).
- **Buyer wants:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Counter at 25% / AUD 6,000,000.**
- **Reason:** 20% is a conditional fallback that needs prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying this draft, and none has been given. Matching the fallback number does not clear it.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket
- **Seller:** De minimis AUD 25,000. Basket AUD 250,000, with only the excess recoverable (a deductible).
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis AUD 5,000. Basket AUD 50,000, with the Seller liable from the first dollar once the basket is exceeded (a tipping basket).
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.**
- **Reason:** Both thresholds are five times our position, and the deductible structure removes recovery of the first AUD 250,000 permanently.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** 18 months. Any limitation also applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months for general claims, with separate periods for Fundamental, Tax and other categories.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Counter at 24 months and delete the "applies to all Claims" default.**
- **Reason:** 18 months is an unauthorised fallback. The blanket default would silently pull Title, Tax and fraud claims into the general limitation period.

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties sit under the general cap and time limits "for administrative simplicity".
- **Buyer wants:** A separate regime with a 100% cap, a period of at least six years, and no general basket, de minimis or knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.**
- **Reason:** Title and capacity go to the core of the deal. Capping them at 20% for 18 months would leave most of the price unprotected if title fails.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance (cl 9.3, 12.8, 20.5) apply to "all Claims of any nature". There is no fraud carve-out.
- **Buyer wants:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions, to the maximum extent enforceable.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Insert an express carve-out.**
- **Reason:** This is non-waivable under our playbook. Nobody, including the deal team, may agree to drop it.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and publicly searchable records (DL 1.1–1.2).
- **Buyer wants:** Specific fair disclosure against identified warranties only.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject DL 1.1 and 1.2. Accept only specific disclosures that are fairly made.**
- **Reason:** Whole-data-room and public-register deemed disclosure would wipe out warranty protection for anything buried in the data room.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** No claim for any matter known to the Buyer or its advisers, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- **Buyer wants:** Delete the clause. Any knowledge qualifier must run to named Seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry, and must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation:** **Delete cl 8.3.**
- **Reason:** A blanket, constructive buyer-knowledge bar reverses the risk allocation and would gut the specific indemnities (for example, Ironquay).

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours only. The condition is treated as satisfied when Bluefen's written consent is delivered. The Seller says the consent is "addressed", but DL para 2 confirms there is no final consent and no evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions have been met.
- **Buyer wants:** An effective consent plus evidence that its conditions are satisfied, both as Conditions Precedent before Completion. Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m, or roughly 30% of FY26 revenue.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Make an effective consent with conditions satisfied a hard CP.**
- **Reason:** For a customer this material, consent-on-delivery and reasonable endeavours alone are insufficient. The Seller's own disclosure contradicts its claim that the matter is "addressed".

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** About AUD 3.2m outstanding, with a release to be provided after Completion. DL para 3 confirms the facility is unpaid and no discharge is in hand.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - A current payout letter.
  - Direct repayment out of Completion funds.
  - Effective security releases delivered at Completion.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.**
- **Reason:** A post-Completion release would leave Riverlark's security over the target after we have paid. A post-Completion release is only acceptable with an irrevocable bank undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval, and neither has been offered.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** The DD-005 bonuses of AUD 420,000 are "a matter for the Seller" and are not itemised in the funds flow. On-costs are not addressed (DL para 5).
- **Buyer wants:** A specific funds-flow line item, or express Seller funding, covering the AUD 420,000 plus any triggered payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the silent exclusion. Add a line item or deduction, plus an indemnity for on-costs.**
- **Reason:** These are Company liabilities triggered by Completion. Leaving them out of the funds flow shifts them to us after Completion.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and is "considered adequate" (cl 11.1).
- **Buyer wants:** A broader indemnity covering ownership and transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials and third-party IP claims, while keeping the SOW3 cure (payment of the fees and a confirmatory assignment).
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the narrow form. Broaden the indemnity.**
- **Reason:** Under DD-004 cl 7.3, IP transfer depends on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee, and there is no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment on file. Note that the AUD 180,000 open amount (DD-010) has not been independently verified either way, so it should not be treated as the confirmed exposure or the confirmed cure amount.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material."
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Preservation of logs.
  - A proper investigation.
  - Regular updates to the Buyer before Completion.
  - Appropriate warranty and indemnity coverage.
- **Recommendation:** **Do not accept the "not material" characterisation. Add investigation and update covenants.**
- **Reason:** The facts are unresolved. On current information there is no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or loss figure, and we should not assert one in either direction. That uncertainty is why we need protection, not reassurance.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Ordinary-course operating costs (DL para 8 makes no statement on whether they are unavoidable, terminable or accrued).
- **Buyer wants:** An assessment of the three related renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) covering timing, scope, terminability and accrual.
- **Recommendation:** **Neither accept nor reject yet. Raise diligence questions.**
- **Reason:** The record does not yet support "ordinary course". Equally, we should not automatically classify the renewals as Debt or seek a price deduction without the facts.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** Uniform limitations for "all Claims", with Tax, IP and Title folded into the general regime (cl 12.3/13, 9.3/12.8/20.5).
- **Buyer wants:** Title, Tax, IP, payment obligations and covenants kept as separate categories, with no hidden override from the general regime.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Add express category-specific carve-outs.**
- **Reason:** The "unless expressly stated otherwise" default is a hidden override that would collapse all protections down to the weakest one.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title is evidenced by the share register at DD-012.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent evidence of title, ownership, absence of encumbrances and authority, for example:
  - ASIC searches.
  - PPSR searches.
  - Share certificates.
  - Board and shareholder approvals.
  - Encumbrance releases, including any linked to Riverlark.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject reliance on DD-012 alone.**
- **Reason:** DD-012 is an internal source supplied by the Seller, not independent proof. The Seller's own DL para 10 acknowledges that the Buyer has not verified title.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP positions are "settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer wants:** These terms treated as open, with no assumption of unlimited liability and no assumption that they are resolved.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject "settled". Keep Tax and IP as open, separately negotiated items.**
- **Reason:** No agreement has been reached through our authority process. Calling them "settled" is an assertion, not a verified update.

## Summary and next steps
1. **All 16 items remain open.** None of the Seller's positions is cleared, and the "FINAL / agreed at principal level" framing should be expressly rejected in our cover note.
2. **Hard non-negotiables to flag in the mark-up:** the fraud carve-out (N-005), the separate Fundamental/Title regime (N-004), and removal of the blanket buyer-knowledge bar (N-007).
3. **Completion mechanics needing immediate action:**
   - Bluefen: effective consent and evidence its conditions are met (N-008).
   - Riverlark: payout letter and security releases (N-009).
   - Bonuses: funds-flow line item including on-costs (N-010).
4. **Escalation:** If the team wants to use any fallback, such as the 20% cap or the 18-month period, it must first get Amelia Frost's written authority identifying this draft.
5. **Diligence requests:**
   - Sandbar renewal terms (N-013).
   - Ironquay payment status and assignment (N-011).
   - Status updates on the DD-006 investigation (N-012).
   - Independent title evidence (N-015).
